Effective Term & Year Select the term and year in which you intend the specialization to become effective. If the selected effective term has passed the applicable deadline by the time the proposal reaches the Faculty Senate, it will automatically be updated to the next available term.
First Graduation Term Select the term and year in which you anticipate the first students will graduate with this credential.
Level Select the level of the specialization: Undergraduate, Graduate, or Dual Dual applies to ABMs and 4+1 specializations.
🔽 The following field will appear only if Dual is chosen for Level.
Dual Type Refer to the linked pages above to understand the difference between ABMs & 4+1s
Academic Calendar Select the academic calendar for the specialization: Accelerated 7-week through URI Online, or Traditional 14-week with Summer and J-Term Sessions (must coincide with parent program).
College Select the college in which the program is housed.
Department Select the department in which the program is housed.

Is this interdisciplinary? The intent of this question is to identify whether the parent program of this specialization is jointly owned by multiple academic departments. If yes, the percentage of ownership assigned to each department must be provided in the curriculum worksheet.

Additional Department(s) and College(s) Enter departments sharing ownership of this program.
Academic Specialization Title Enter the title of the specialization. See the linked page for title formatting guidelines.
Specialization Description List the requirements of the specialization. Only specialization-specific requirements should be listed here, and no program requirements should be duplicated.
Admission Requirements If the specialization has specific admission requirements, list them here. Otherwise, enter: “See admission requirements for {Program Title}.”
Total specialization credits (excluding program credits) Enter the number of credits required for this specialization.

Total double-counted course credits Enter the number of credits double counted towards this ABM.

Faculty Senate Executive Committee

Through RI General Law §16-32-10, academic responsibility at URI is delegated to the President and the Faculty Senate. The Faculty Senate Executive Committee (FSEC) serves as the steering committee of the Senate. It represents the Senate in meetings with other University bodies and with the Provost, the President, and the URI Board of Trustees. Meetings of the FSEC are held weekly to coordinate the Senate’s business and its committees and address concerns within its jurisdiction.
For the description of the powers and duties of the Executive Committee, please see University Manual Appendix C: By-laws of the Faculty Senate, Section 4.1 – 4.9.

Kuali Curriculum Management (CM) is the system used at URI to manage university-wide curricula, the curriculum approval process, and the official academic catalog.

Kuali CM is the cloud-based system used to manage the curriculum approval process through forms and workflow.
The URI Academic Catalog is built in Kuali and pulls information directly from all course, program, and specialization records.
Kuali CM integrates with eCampus . When a course is approved in Kuali, the information is sent to eCampus and updated for a future term.

Information entered into Kuali curricular forms (course, program, and specialization proposals) flows directly into the catalog and eCampus. It is essential that proposals are written clearly and leave no room for interpretation.

Access to Kuali CM is limited to faculty, Deans, and select administrators and staff. Only faculty members are permitted to submit proposals.
To request access or learn how to log in, visit the Faculty Senate’s Kuali Access page.

The Committee for Research and Creative Activities (henceforth referred to as the “full committee”) shall consist of six faculty senators and five non-senator research-active faculty) and students active, experienced, or concerned with various aspects of research, creative, and scholarly efforts at URI. The Vice President for Research and Economic Development (VPRED) shall be an ex officio (non-voting) member of the committee. The FSEC shall appoint six senators, and the VPRED shall appoint five research-active non- senators. #23-24-21

The full committee shall serve as the representative voice of the university community in all matters related to research, creative, and scholarly activities. It shall seek to improve the environment for research at URI in all ways possible. The Chair of the full committee shall serve as an ex-officio voting member of the Intellectual Property Committee (See University Manual section 5.30.10). The full committee shall form from its membership, a subcommittee, the Competitive Grants Subcommittee, the chair of which shall be appointed from the members of the full committee. The full committee shall meet at least once a month and present reports to the Faculty Senate in December and April and more often as needed. The Competitive Grants Subcommittee shall report to the Faculty Senate at least once annually. #17-18-18, #21-22-37 , #23-24-21, #24-25-19

The Curriculum and Standards Committee (CASC)

The Curriculum and Standards Committee shall comprise six or more faculty members one of whom serves as the chairperson of the General Education committee. The chair of the General Education Committee shall be appointed from the members of the committee. The committee shall consider and make recommendations to the Faculty Senate on the items specifically assigned to it (see By-laws 4.21 to 4.25). The committee shall meet at least once a month and present reports to the Faculty Senate as often as necessary. Joint meetings of the Curriculum and Standards and General Education curriculum committees shall occur early fall and late spring to review and calibrate standards for course review. #17-18-12, #20-21-14 , #21-22-37

The General Education Committee (GEC)

The General Education Committee shall comprise six or more members, one of whom is the chair of the Curriculum and Standards committee. The committee shall study and make recommendations on the establishment, modification or abolition of General Education requirements for graduation to be applicable to degree candidates; consider new and existing courses proposed for general education; evaluate the effectiveness of the general education program; maintain liaison with the University administration for effective implementation of approved recommendations; and cooperate closely with the Director of General Education (see University Manual section 8.20.30). The Curriculum and Standards Committee and the General Education Committee shall maintain consistent standards by which courses are reviewed. #17-18-12, #20-21-14, #21-22-6, #21-22-37

Constitution, By-Laws, and University Manual Committee (CBUM)

Constitution, By-laws, and University Manual Committee shall comprise four or more members. This committee shall review the operation of University governance and propose changes in the Constitution and By-Laws of the Faculty Senate and in the University Manual; review proposals for changes in University governance from whatever source and make recommendations concerning them to the Faculty Senate and to the other appropriate bodies and individuals; construe the meaning of the Constitution, the By-Laws and the University Manual upon the request of the Senate President or Executive Committee, any senator or member of the General Faculty, or the President; assure that all duly approved changes are incorporated into the Constitution and By-Laws and into the University Manual, and that no unauthorized changes are made in these instruments; and assure that the language of all duly approved changes is consistent with the style, format and arrangement of the Constitution and By-Laws and of the University Manual. #17-18-12 , #20-21-5 , #20-21-14, #20-21-36, #21-22-37
